reading: The 3x3 input is scaled to a 3x3 grid of 3x3 blocks; block (i,j) is a copy of the input where input cell (i,j) is non-background, otherwise empty.
why: every output block is either the input or all background, and it is the input exactly where the input cell is fg
invariants: block contents are the unchanged input

reading: The 6-row input is a vertical repeat of a short row pattern; the pattern is continued to 9 rows and colour 1 becomes 2.

slots.period: smallest row period p with row[i] = row[i-p] in the input (2, 4, 3 in the pairs)
slots.length: output height 9 = 1.5 x input height; width unchanged

why: output row i = input row (i mod p) with 1 recoloured to 2, for i in 0..8

reading: Objects resting on the bottom are taken left to right and chained diagonally from the top-left corner: the first object's box is placed at (0,0) and each next object's top-left cell goes on the previous object's bottom-right cell, later objects drawn over earlier ones.

slots.subjects: the 4-connected single-colour objects, ordered by left column
slots.step: next top-left = previous object's bottom-right corner (overlap one cell, later wins)

why: every object keeps its shape and colour; boxes overlap only at chained corners

reading: A 3x3 main shape has small marker pieces one gap away on some sides; the main shape is repeated in each marker's direction with step 4 (3 + gap) until the border, each copy in that marker's colour.

slots.unit: the largest object (3x3 box), its shape
slots.directions: each other object marks a 3x3 box offset by 4*(dy,dx) from the unit, dy,dx in {-1,0,1}

why: copies at offsets 4k*(dy,dx), k>=1, are exact recoloured copies of the unit's shape; the unit itself unchanged

reading: The grid holds a regular array of identical tiles corrupted by noise cells; every tile is replaced by the cell-wise majority tile and everything outside the tiles is cleared.

slots.tiles: the regular array of equal-size boxes (rows/columns separated by background gaps)
slots.unit: cell-wise majority vote over all tiles
slots.rest: all cells outside tiles become background

why: every output tile equals the majority tile; output is background outside the tile array

reading: Like a self-tile: block (i,j) of the 9x9 output is filled where input cell (i,j) is fg, but the block is the colour-inverted input (fg cells become 0, 0 cells become the fg colour).

slots.unit: the input with its single fg colour and background swapped
slots.extent: blocks whose input cell is fg (as tile extent=fg)

why: every output block is either the inverted input or all background, inverted exactly where the input cell is fg
invariants: only the input's one fg colour appears

reading: A lattice of separator lines holds 2x2 coloured cells; background cells lying between two cells of the same colour on one row or column are filled with that colour, separator lines left intact.

new_rows.name: between_same
new_rows.datalog:
width(max(X)) :- px(Y, X, C).
rowcnt(Y, C, count(X)) :- cell(Y, X, C).
linecol(C) :- rowcnt(Y, C, N), width(W), N = W + 1.
bgc(Y, X) :- px(Y, X, C), !cell(Y, X, C).
hb(Y, X) :- bgc(Y, X), cell(Y, X1, C), cell(Y, X2, C), !linecol(C), X1 < X, X < X2.
vb(Y, X) :- bgc(Y, X), cell(Y1, X, C), cell(Y2, X, C), !linecol(C), Y1 < Y, Y < Y2.
between_same(Y, X) :- hb(Y, X).
between_same(Y, X) :- vb(Y, X).

slots.own: the colour C of the same-colour pair that brackets the cell

why: each filled cell is background with a same (non-separator) colour on both sides in its row or column; no other cell changes

reading: Separator lines cut the grid into 3x3 panels of 3x3 cells; the one panel with the fewest coloured cells (4) is enlarged so that each panel is filled entirely with the colour of the corresponding cell of that panel (0 where it is empty).

slots.panels: the 3x3 panels cut by full separator lines (colour 5)
slots.chosen: the panel with the fewest non-background cells

why: every output panel is uniform and its colour equals the chosen panel's cell at that panel's position

reading: Each small plus (centre colour A, arms colour B) grows into a star: the arms extend to length 2 in colour B and diagonals of length 2 are drawn from the centre in colour A.

slots.subjects: each plus-shaped object (its centre cell and 4 arm cells)
slots.orthogonal: cells at distance 1..2 in the 4 axis directions get the arm colour
slots.diagonal: cells at distance 1..2 in the 4 diagonal directions get the centre colour

why: every star is a 5x5 pattern centred on the plus centre; other cells unchanged

reading: Blobs of 1 joined by thin paths each contain one seed cell of another colour; every 1-cell whose 8 neighbours are all non-background (inside the grid) takes the seed colour of its connected blob.

new_rows.name: interior
new_rows.datalog:
inb(Y, X) :- px(Y, X, C).
bgc(Y, X) :- px(Y, X, C), !cell(Y, X, C).
edge(Y, X) :- cell(Y, X, C), off(DY, DX), Y2 = Y + DY, X2 = X + DX, bgc(Y2, X2).
edge(Y, X) :- cell(Y, X, C), off(DY, DX), Y2 = Y + DY, X2 = X + DX, !inb(Y2, X2).
interior(Y, X) :- cell(Y, X, C), !edge(Y, X).

slots.own: the one non-1 colour in the cell's 8-connected non-background component (not the nearest seed: that fails)

why: exactly the fg cells with all 8 neighbours fg change, to their component's seed colour
